stories.headline: Apple Names Johny Srouji Chief Hardware Officer, Reorganizes Hardware Into Five Groups

key_facts.fact: Apple promoted Johny Srouji to the newly created role of Chief Hardware Officer, effective April 20, combining hardware engineering and hardware technologies divisions under one organization.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple today announced that, effective immediately, Apple executive Johny Srouji will become chief hardware officer.

key_facts.fact: Srouji organized the combined division into five areas: hardware engineering (Tom Marieb, ex-Intel), silicon (Sri Santhanam, 18-year veteran), advanced technologies (Zongjian Chen), platform architecture (Tim Millet, 21-year veteran), and program management (Donny Nordhues).
key_facts.excerpt: Srouji will organize the combined hardware engineering and hardware technologies group into five areas: Hardware engineering: Overseen by Tom Marieb... Silicon: Overseen by Sri Santhanam... Advanced technologies: Overseen by Zongjian Chen... Platform architecture: Overseen by Tim Millet... Project management: Overseen by Donny Nordhues.

key_facts.fact: The restructuring accompanies the announcement that John Ternus will succeed Tim Cook as Apple CEO on September 1, with Cook becoming executive chairman.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of Apple's reorganization elevating John Ternus to CEO, the company also promoted Johny Srouji to a broader new chief hardware officer role.

key_facts.fact: Srouji joined Apple in 2008 to lead development of the A4, Apple's first custom system-on-a-chip, after senior positions at Intel and IBM in processor design.
key_facts.excerpt: Srouji joined Apple in 2008 to lead development of A4, the first Apple-designed system-on-a-chip. Prior to Apple, Srouji held senior positions at Intel and IBM in the area of processor development and design.

key_facts.fact: The reorganization returns Apple to an earlier model used under former hardware chief Bob Mansfield, when hardware operated as a single unit; it was later split, allowing Ternus and Srouji to rise through separate divisions.
key_facts.excerpt: The move marks a return to an earlier organizational model used more than a decade ago, when Apple's hardware teams operated as a single unit under former hardware chief Bob Mansfield.

stories.headline: Amazon Invests Up to $25B in Anthropic; Anthropic Commits $100B+ on AWS for 5GW of Trainium

key_facts.fact: Amazon will invest $5 billion in Anthropic immediately, with up to $20 billion more tied to commercial milestones, bringing total potential investment to $33 billion on top of $8 billion already invested since 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon will invest $5 billion in Anthropic now, and an additional $20 billion in the future, subject to certain commercial milestones. This is in addition to the $8 billion Amazon previously invested in the company.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic committed to spending more than $100 billion over the next 10 years on AWS technologies, securing up to 5 gigawatts of compute capacity across Trainium2, Trainium3, and Trainium4 chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced on Monday (April 20) that it has signed a massive new agreement with Amazon, committing to spend more than $100 billion on AWS over the next decade in exchange for up to 5 gigawatts of computing capacity.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 1 gigawatt of Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity is expected to come online by end of 2026; Anthropic already uses over 1 million Trainium2 chips through Project Rainier.
key_facts.excerpt: End of 2026: Nearly 1GW total of Trainium2 and Trainium3... Anthropic already uses more than 1 million Trainium2 chips to train and serve Claude through Project Rainier — one of the largest AI compute clusters in the world.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's run-rate revenue has hit $30 billion, up from roughly $9 billion at end of 2025, with over 100,000 customers running Claude on Amazon Bedrock.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic disclosed that its run-rate revenue has hit $30 billion, up from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025... More than 100,000 customers now run Claude on Amazon Bedrock.

key_facts.fact: Combined with a separate Google/Broadcom deal for 4.5GW of TPU capacity, Anthropic now has commitments for nearly 10GW of AI compute across two major cloud platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic now has commitments for up to 5GW from AWS plus 4.5GW from Google/Broadcom — nearly 10GW of AI compute locked in across two major cloud platforms.

stories.headline: Nvidia PCB Supplier Victory Giant Surges ~60% in $2.2B Hong Kong IPO Debut

key_facts.fact: Victory Giant Technology Huizhou shares rocketed 59.6% in early trade to HK$335, having priced its IPO at HK$209.88 and raising HK$17.3 billion (~US$2.2 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: Shares in the Guangdong-based firm rocketed 59.6 per cent in early trade to HK$335, having set its price at HK$209.88 and raising HK$17.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: The IPO is Hong Kong's largest this year, surpassing debuts from Chinese AI startups Zhipu AI, MiniMax, and chip firms Biren Technology and OmniVision.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial public offering (IPO) is the biggest since Zijin Gold International raised US$3.7 billion in September. It is also the latest in a recent run of blockbuster debuts from Chinese AI-related companies in Hong Kong.

key_facts.fact: Victory Giant makes high-end printed circuit boards (PCBs), a crucial component of AI servers, with Nvidia as one of its key customers. The company is already listed in Shenzhen.
key_facts.excerpt: Victory Giant, whose shares are already listed across the border in Shenzhen, makes high-end printed circuit boards (PCBs), a crucial component of AI servers. One of its key customers is Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: The company will use most IPO proceeds to expand production in mainland China as Beijing accelerates efforts to boost domestic semiconductor-adjacent manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: Victory Giant Technology Huizhou has said it will use most of the proceeds to expand production in mainland China. It comes as the country races to boost domestic production of the microchips used to train and power generative AI tools.

key_facts.fact: Pepperstone strategist Dilin Wu noted that tight supply in high-end PCB manufacturing benefits companies like Victory Giant, which gain from both policy support and financing accessibility.
key_facts.excerpt: 'China continues to prioritise AI infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, and semiconductor-adjacent supply chains as strategic sectors,' Dilin Wu, research strategist at Pepperstone, told AFP. 'The current cycle is still characterised by tight supply in high-end PCB manufacturing.'

stories.headline: Humble Unveils Fully Electric Cabless Autonomous Truck, Exits Stealth With $24M Seed

key_facts.fact: Humble unveiled the Humble Hauler, a fully electric cabless autonomous truck designed for the U.S. freight industry, coming out of stealth mode.
key_facts.excerpt: Startup Humble debuts cabless autonomous truck targeting $900 billion U.S. freight industry

key_facts.fact: The company raised a $24 million seed round led by Eclipse Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: Humble CEO Eyal Cohen built the prototype for his autonomous truck in six months.

key_facts.fact: The cabless design eliminates the driver cabin entirely, targeting the $900 billion U.S. freight industry with a purpose-built autonomous-first form factor.
key_facts.excerpt: Startup Humble debuts cabless autonomous truck targeting $900 billion U.S. freight industry

stories.headline: CFIUS Blocks Chinese LED Maker Sanan's $239M Acquisition of Dutch Firm Lumileds

key_facts.fact: China's leading LED chipmaker Sanan Optoelectronics and its Malaysian partner withdrew their US$239 million all-cash offer to acquire Lumileds Holding after CFIUS concluded the deal posed 'irresolvable U.S. national security risks.'
key_facts.excerpt: CFIUS concluded the deal would pose 'irresolvable U.S. national security risks' and requested that the parties withdraw their application and terminate the transaction.

key_facts.fact: No equity transfer payment had been made and the target shares had not been delivered; Sanan said the termination will not materially affect its operations or financial position.
key_facts.excerpt: As of the transaction's termination, no equity transfer payment had been made and the target shares had not been delivered or settled. Sanan Optoelectronics stated in its announcement that the termination does not trigger any breach of contract.

key_facts.fact: Lumileds ranks third globally in automotive lighting LED revenue behind ams OSRAM and Nichia, and is part of Apple's smartphone flash LED supply chain.
key_facts.excerpt: It ranks third globally in automotive lighting LED revenue, behind only ams OSRAM and Nichia. In smartphone flash LEDs, it is part of Apple's supply chain, ranking just below Nichia.

key_facts.fact: Sanan had planned to use Lumileds' manufacturing facilities in Singapore and Malaysia to strengthen its overseas production capacity and global customer supply.
key_facts.excerpt: The move was aimed at quickly securing overseas production capacity and strengthening supply for global customers by leveraging Lumileds' manufacturing facilities in Singapore and Malaysia.

sources.title: Chinese LED Leader Sanan's $239M Acquisition of Dutch Firm Lumileds Falls Through Amid U.S. Pushback

stories.headline: Wärtsilä Wins 412 MW Gas Engine Order for Off-Grid Ohio Hyperscale Data Center

key_facts.fact: Wärtsilä received an order to supply 412 MW of gas engine power for a major hyperscale data center in Ohio, using 40 Wärtsilä 34SG spark-ignited gas engines.
key_facts.excerpt: Technology group Wärtsilä has received an order to supply 412 MW of engine power to support a major new hyperscale data center project in Ohio, United States. The project includes 40 Wärtsilä 34SG (spark gas) engines.

key_facts.fact: The order brings Wärtsilä's total engine capacity sold into the US data center market to over 1.6 GW; this is the company's fourth US data center order.
key_facts.excerpt: This order brings Wärtsilä's total engine capacity sold into the US data center market to over 1.6 GW... This is Wärtsilä's fourth data center related order in the USA.

key_facts.fact: The power plant will operate off-grid as primary power, enabling the data center to avoid long grid interconnection delays common to the US market, with commercial operation expected by early 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The power plant will provide highly flexible, primary power, enabling the data center to operate off-grid and avoid long interconnection delays common to the US market. Equipment deliveries are scheduled to align with an anticipated commercial operation date of early 2028.

key_facts.fact: This is the first deployment of Wärtsilä's proven 34SG engine model in a data center application; the modular design scales up to 500MW+.
key_facts.excerpt: This latest order marks the first use of the highly proven 34SG model in a data center application... Its modular design accommodates data center developers looking for power solutions that can be deployed in modular blocks, scaling up to 500MW+.

sources.title: Wärtsilä's 34SG engine makes its data center debut with new 412 MW U.S. project

stories.headline: BMW Expands Humanoid Robot Program to German EV Factory After Building 30K+ Vehicles in US Pilot

key_facts.fact: BMW is deploying Hexagon Robotics' AEON humanoid robots at its Leipzig, Germany factory for EV production, after a successful pilot at its Spartanburg, South Carolina plant.
key_facts.excerpt: After a successful pilot in Spartanburg, South Carolina, BMW is bringing that same idea into its Leipzig, Germany, factory, where it is testing robots in real production environments. This time, it is partnering with Hexagon Robotics to introduce a new generation of AI-powered machines.

key_facts.fact: BMW's earlier pilot used Figure 02 humanoid robots for precise sheet metal positioning on the X3 production line, contributing to building more than 30,000 vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: BMW's earlier pilot used Figure 02 humanoid robots for a very specific task. They handled the precise positioning of sheet metal for welding on the BMW X3 production line... According to BMW, those robots helped contribute to building more than 30,000 vehicles.

key_facts.fact: The AEON robots use AI-based motion control and real-time sensors to adapt to their environment without constant human direction, which Hexagon calls 'Physical AI.'
key_facts.excerpt: They rely on AI-based motion control, which helps them move through complex spaces. At the same time, built-in sensors allow them to understand their surroundings in real time... Hexagon refers to this as 'Physical AI.'

key_facts.fact: BMW executive Michael Nikolaides framed the deployment as part of the company's broader iFACTORY initiative for digitalization and production competitiveness.
key_facts.excerpt: Michael Nikolaides, who oversees BMW's production network, says these pilot programs help the company refine how AI-powered robots learn on the job... 'Digitalization improves the competitiveness... opens up entirely new possibilities in production.'

sources.title: BMW expands humanoid robot program to Germany after Spartanburg success
